I am 76 years old and I have only been doing this for one year. I have no schooling. What I know, I learned from watching my neighbors and asking the man at the supply shop in town.

My land is 5.5 mu. I grow wheat and maize on the same 3 mu, one after the other — wheat in the cold months, maize in the summer. The other 2.5 mu I put in cotton. That is what the people around me do, so I do the same.

For the **wheat**, I will plant in October after I turn the soil with the rotary machine — I hire someone with a small machine to do it, I cannot do it myself. I will buy the improved variety from the supply shop, whatever the man there recommends. I will water it three times: once before winter sets in, once when it starts growing again in spring, and once when the heads are filling. I put down fertilizer at planting and again in spring. I use what my neighbor told me — about a bag of urea and some compound fertilizer per mu.

For the **maize**, right after I harvest the wheat in June I will plant directly into the stubble — my neighbor said I don't need to plow again. I will use the hybrid seeds in the small yellow packet, that is what everyone uses. I water twice if the rain is not enough. I spray once for the corn borer and once for weeds.

For the **cotton**, this is the hardest work and I am old. I will plant in late April on the other field. Cotton needs many sprayings — last year I was told to spray five or six times for bugs. I will do the same this year. I water four times and use fertilizer several times through the season. My hands are not fast but I will manage with my household member helping.

I do not try anything new. I do what worked last year and what my neighbors do. I just want a steady harvest.
